statement: Prove that a space X is connected if and only if the only subsets that are both open and closed are the empty set and X.
solution: If A is clopen with ∅≠A≠X, then X=A∪(X\A) is a separation, so X is disconnected. Conversely a separation X=U∪V into disjoint nonempty opens makes U clopen (its complement V is open) with ∅≠U≠X. So no nontrivial clopen sets iff connected.

statement: Prove that X is connected if and only if there is no continuous surjection from X onto the two-point discrete space {0,1}.
solution: A continuous surjection f:X→{0,1} gives a separation X=f^{-1}(0)∪f^{-1}(1) into disjoint nonempty opens, so X disconnected. Conversely a separation X=U∪V defines such a surjection (0 on U, 1 on V), which is continuous since preimages of the four subsets of {0,1} are ∅,U,V,X, all open.

statement: Prove that R with the standard topology is connected.
solution: Suppose R=A∪B is a separation with a∈A, b∈B, a<b. Let c=sup{x∈[a,b] : [a,x]⊆A}. For x<c there is s∈S above x with [a,s]⊆A, so [a,c)⊆A; since A is closed, c∈A, giving [a,c]⊆A and c<b (as b∈B). But A is open, so (c-ε,c+ε)⊆A for some ε>0, whence [a,c+ε')⊆A for a small ε'>0 with c+ε'<b — contradicting c=sup. Hence R has no separation and is connected.

statement: Prove that the connected subsets of R are exactly the intervals (including rays and R itself).
solution: If C is not an interval, there are a<c<b with a,b∈C, c∉C; then C∩(-∞,c) and C∩(c,∞) form a separation, so C is disconnected. Conversely an interval is connected by the same sup argument as for R (cn03): any separation yields a supremum point lying in the wrong piece.

statement: Prove that if A is connected and A ⊆ B ⊆ cl(A), then B is connected.
solution: Suppose B=U∪V is a separation into disjoint nonempty relatively-open sets. Since A is connected, A lies in one piece, say A⊆U. Pick v∈V; write V=B∩W with W open in X, so W is a neighborhood of v. Since v∈B⊆cl(A), W meets A at some point a∈A⊆U. But a∈W and a∈B, so a∈B∩W=V, giving a∈U∩V=∅ — a contradiction. Hence V=∅, so B is connected.

statement: Prove that the union of a collection of connected subspaces with a common point is connected.
solution: Let {A_i} be connected with common point p, and A=∪A_i. Suppose A=U∪V is a separation with p∈U. Each A_i is connected and meets U (contains p), so A_i⊆U. Then A⊆U and V=∅, a contradiction. Hence A is connected.

statement: Prove that the product of two connected spaces is connected.
solution: Let X,Y be connected, fix (a,b). For each x, the slice {x}×Y is homeomorphic to Y (connected), and X×{b} is connected; their union T_x=(X×{b})∪({x}×Y) is connected (common point (x,b)). All T_x share (a,b), so X×Y=∪_x T_x is connected by cn06.

statement: Prove that the connected components of a space are connected, pairwise disjoint, and cover the space.
solution: Define x~y if some connected set contains both. This is an equivalence relation (reflexive via {x}; symmetric trivially; transitive by cn06 gluing at the shared point). Its classes (components) partition X. Each class is the union of all connected sets through a point, connected by cn06.

statement: Prove that connected components are closed.
solution: Let C be a component and x∈C. cl(C) is connected (cn05 with B=cl(C)) and contains C, so cl(C) is a connected set containing x, hence cl(C)⊆C by maximality of the component. Thus C=cl(C) is closed.

statement: Prove that every path-connected space is connected.
solution: Suppose X path-connected but X=U∪V a separation. Pick a∈U,b∈V and a path p:[0,1]→X from a to b. Then p([0,1]) is connected (continuous image of connected [0,1]) yet meets both U and V, giving a separation of a connected set — contradiction. So X is connected.

statement: Prove the Intermediate Value Theorem using connectedness: a continuous f: [a,b] → R takes every value between f(a) and f(b).
solution: [a,b] is connected, so f([a,b]) is connected in R, hence an interval (cn04). An interval containing f(a) and f(b) contains everything between them, so every intermediate value is attained.

statement: Prove that the continuous image of a path-connected space is path-connected.
solution: Let f:X→Y continuous, X path-connected. Given f(x0),f(x1)∈f(X), take a path p from x0 to x1 in X; then f∘p is a continuous path in Y from f(x0) to f(x1). So f(X) is path-connected.

statement: Prove that a discrete space with more than one point is disconnected.
solution: Pick a point x; in the discrete topology {x} and X\{x} are both open, nonempty, disjoint, and cover X, giving a separation. Hence X is disconnected.

statement: Prove that Q, the rationals with the subspace topology from R, is totally disconnected (its only connected subsets are singletons and the empty set).
solution: Let C⊆Q have two points a<b. Choose an irrational r with a<r<b. Then C∩(-∞,r) and C∩(r,∞) are disjoint nonempty relatively-open sets covering C, a separation. So no connected subset of Q has more than one point.

statement: Prove that the component of a point x is the union of all connected subsets of X that contain x.
solution: Let C_x be that union. Each set in the union contains x, so by cn06 (common point x) C_x is connected. It is the largest connected set containing x, which is exactly the component of x by definition.

statement: Prove that the relation 'there is a path from x to y' is an equivalence relation.
solution: Reflexive: the constant path at x. Symmetric: reverse a path p by t↦p(1-t), still continuous. Transitive: concatenate paths p,q by running p on [0,1/2] and q on [1/2,1]; the result is continuous by the pasting lemma on the two closed halves (they agree at 1/2).

statement: Prove that if {C_n} is a sequence of connected subsets with C_n ∩ C_{n+1} nonempty for all n, then the union is connected.
solution: Let U_1=C_1, U_{n+1}=U_n∪C_{n+1}. By induction each U_n is connected: U_n∪C_{n+1} is a union of two connected sets sharing a point of C_n∩C_{n+1}, connected by cn06. All U_n contain C_1, so their union ∪C_n=∪U_n is connected by cn06.

statement: Prove that if f: X → Y is continuous and X is connected, then the graph {(x, f(x))} is connected.
solution: The graph map g(x)=(x,f(x)) is continuous (c11) and its image is the graph. A continuous image of the connected space X is connected, so the graph is connected.
